To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
particular combinations of immunoglobulin GM and/or KM allotypes are associated with the outcome (clearance versus persistence) of hepatitis C virus infection.
the outcome of HVC infection is influenced by epistatic interactions among the immunoglobulin genes on chromosomes 2 and 14.
the immunoglobulin GM and/or KM allotypes are associated with clearance or persistence of hepatitis C virus infection, but only when they occur together with other allotypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of the immune response to infectious diseases and with the development of vaccines against infectious agents.
understanding genetic factors that affect the outcome of HVC infection.
the identification of genetic factors that affect susceptibility to infection, disease progression, and outcome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GM 1, 3, 17 23 1,5 13 phenotype is associated with clearance of hepatitis C virus infection and the GM 1, 3, 5, 13 23 phenotype with persistence of the infection.
GM and KM phenotypes are associated with HCV infection, and that the presence of certain GM phenotypes (GM 1,17,5,13) and absence of KM 1 or KM 3 (or both) are associated with clearance of infection.
the genetic markers of immunoglobulins (GM and KM allotypes) are associated with outcome of HCV infections and the association is due to the epistatic interactions among these markers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCV is a complex disease, with many genes and many environmental factors that interact to determine outcome.
the GM 1,5,13 23 and KM 1 phenotypes are associated with the clearance and the GM 1 3 17 23 13 phenotype is associated with persistence of HCV.
the presence of certain immunoglobulin allotypes (GM 1,17, KM 1) and the absence of others (GM 3,13, KM 3) are associated with the clearance and persistence of infection, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the outcome of HAV and HCV infections are influenced by genetic markers of the humoral response to infection.
the immune response to HCV is influenced by genetic markers on chromosomes 14 and 2.
genetic markers of the immune system can be used to identify persons at high and low risk of developing a chronic HCV infection.
